structural-causal.name: alignment2036
structural-causal.basis: AI/cloud scaling raises optical bandwidth and energy-efficiency requirements.

structural-causal.name: bottleneckControl
structural-causal.basis: InP lasers and optical components are enabling inputs to high-bandwidth data-center links.

structural-causal.name: scenarioRobustness
structural-causal.basis: Current FY2026 growth supports the thesis, while the incremental Greensboro capacity does not ramp until mid-2028.

structural-causal.name: substitutionResilience
structural-causal.basis: Optical intensity can rise while individual component architectures and suppliers remain substitutable.

structural-causal.name: supplyChainResilience
structural-causal.basis: New U.S. InP capacity diversifies/expands supply but introduces fab-ramp and yield risk.

discovery-weak-signals.name: Strategic customer validation
discovery-weak-signals.basis: Purchase commitment, equity investment and capacity-access agreement validate optical bottleneck relevance.

adversarial-red-team.name: financialOperatingMomentum
adversarial-red-team.basis: Operating performance improved strongly, but capital-structure accounting and dilution require separation from operations.

adversarial-red-team.name: substitutionResilience
adversarial-red-team.basis: Optics demand may persist even if specific laser architectures or suppliers change.

adversarial-red-team.name: pricingPower
adversarial-red-team.basis: Strategic commitment validates demand but does not by itself prove durable pricing power.

expectations-execution.name: Execution milestone clarity
expectations-execution.basis: Customer commitment is strong, while meaningful new-fab capacity remains a future execution event.
